en.title: Livonia Residents Raise Accessibility Concerns Ahead of Early Voting
en.summary: Livonia residents raised accessibility concerns at city hall ahead of early voting, citing inadequate wheelchair access, unclear signage, and insufficient voting booth accommodations. Meanwhile, Ontario marked 2026 as a reporting year under the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, and community donations funded ADA‑compliant upgrades at Camp Rainbow. A separate commentary emphasized that news should be accessible to all readers without being mistaken for effortlessness.

highlights.title: Livonia residents raise accessibility concerns at city hall ahead of early voting
2026 Is a Reporting Year Under the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA)
Community generosity creates ADA-accessible improvements at Camp Rainbow
Behind the Bylines: News should be accessible. It should not be effortless

zh-TW.title: 利沃尼亞居民在早期投票前對市政廳無障礙問題提出關注
zh-TW.summary: 利沃尼亞居民在早期投票前對市政廳無障礙問題提出關注，指出輪椅通行不足、標識不明及投票亭缺乏適應性設施。同時，安大略省將2026年指定為殘疾人無障礙法（AODA）報告年，社區捐助為彩虹營創建符合ADA的設施。另一則評論強調新聞應該對所有讀者可及，但不應等同於輕鬆獲得。
